\chapter{Boolean Analysis — General}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpThresholds.General
\section{Overview}
Increasing symmetric Boolean functions and graph properties admit quantitative threshold and approximation statements. Structural statements for finite products describe boosters, pseudo-juntas, and input-dependent notable coordinates.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp Threshold for Transitive Increasing Boolean Functions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.friedgut_kalai_sharp_threshold}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsIncreasing, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsTransitiveSymmetric, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.thresholdCurve}
There is a constant $B>0$ such that for every $n\ge2$ and every increasing, transitively
symmetric function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ that is nonconstant, suppose
$p_c,\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<p_c\le\tfrac12$, the biased probability that
$f=1$ at $p_c$ is $\tfrac12$, and $0<\varepsilon<\tfrac14$. Set
$\displaystyle\eta=B\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)\log(1/p_c)}{\log n}$. If
$\eta\le\tfrac12$, then the biased probability that $f=1$ at $p_c(1-\eta)$ is at most
$\varepsilon$, and at $p_c(1+\eta)$ it is at least $1-\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Graph Sharp-Threshold Approximation by Monotone DNF]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.friedgut_graph_sharp_threshold}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.GraphEdge, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsGraphProperty, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsIncreasing, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsMonotoneDNF, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.biasedProbability, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.biasedTotalInfluence, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width}
There is a function $w:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb N$ with the following
property. For all $v,n\in\mathbb N$, every bijection from the $n$ coordinates to the
two-element subsets of a labeled $v$-vertex set, and every increasing Boolean graph
property $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ invariant under permutations of the vertices, let
$p,K,\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<p\le\tfrac12$, $K>0$, and $0<\varepsilon<1$. If
the biased total influence of $f$ at parameter $p$ is at most $K$, then there is a
monotone DNF formula $d$ of width at most $w(K,\varepsilon)$ whose probability of
disagreement with $f$ under the Bernoulli-$p$ product weights is at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bourgain booster theorem]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.bourgain_sharp_threshold}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.prob, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.variance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsBooster}
There exist positive real constants $C,D$ such that, for every natural number $n$, every
product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, every
real-valued function $f$ taking only the values $-1$ and $1$, and every real $K$ with
$I(f)\leq K$ and $1/100\leq\operatorname{Var}_P(f)$, there is a real number $\tau$ such
that $e^{-CK^2}\leq|\tau|$ and $|\tau|$ is at most the probability of the event that an
outcome $x$ admits a set of coordinates $T$ with $|T|\leq DK$ for which either $\tau>0$
and $\mathbb E_P f+\tau\leq E_Tf(x)$, or $\tau<0$ and $E_Tf(x)\leq\mathbb E_P f+\tau$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hatami pseudo-junta approximation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hatami_pseudo_junta}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.prob, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsPseudoJunta}
There is a constant $C>0$ such that, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, every product $P$ of $n$
finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, every Boolean-valued
function $f$ on its outcome space, and all $K,\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ with $K\ge0$,
total influence $I(f)\le K$, and $\varepsilon>0$, there is a Boolean-valued function $h$
on the same space that is a $\exp(CK^3/\varepsilon^3)$-pseudo-junta and satisfies
$\Pr_P(f\ne h)\le\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence of Boolean pseudo-juntas]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.pseudo_junta_totalInfluence_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsPseudoJunta}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom
masses, and let $h$ take values in $\\{-1,1\}$ on its outcome space. If $h$ is a
$K$-pseudo-junta, meaning its expected number of exposed coordinates is at most $K$,
then its total influence satisfies $I(h)\le 4K$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bourgain notable-coordinate structure]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.bourgain_notable_coordinates}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.notableFamily}
There exist positive real constants $C,D$ such that, for every natural number $n$, every
product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, every
real-valued function $f$ taking only the values $-1$ and $1$, and every $\varepsilon$
with $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, define $k=I(f)/\varepsilon$, where $I(f)$ is the total
influence. There is a choice of a set of coordinates $J(x)$ for each outcome $x$ such
that, for every $x$, $|J(x)|\leq e^{Ck}$ and the number of subsets $S\subseteq J(x)$
with $|S|\leq k$ is at most $e^{Dk^2}$; moreover, the expectation of the sum of squared
components $f_S(x)^2$ over all subsets $S\subseteq[n]$ not in that family is at most
$2\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized Laplacian estimate off notable coordinates]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.nonnotable_randomized_laplacian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.notableCoordinates, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces
whose coordinate atom weights are strictly positive and sum to one, and let
$\Omega=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}\Omega_j$ be its outcome space. For $f\colon\Omega\to\mathbb
R$, $x\in\Omega$, a coordinate $i$, and $\tau>0$, suppose $i$ is not notable at $x$,
meaning $\tau>\sum_{S\ni i}f_S(x)^2$, where $f_S$ is the $S$-component of $f$. Set
$g=T_{2/5}L_i f$ and $h(r)=\sum_S\chi_S(r)g_S(x)$ for $r\in\{0,1\}^n$, using the product
spectral noise and components and the Walsh characters on the Boolean cube. Then, with
cube power means taken under the uniform measure,
$\|T_{1/\sqrt3}h\|_2^2\le\tau^{1/3}\|h\|_{4/3}^{4/3}$.
\end{theorem}
